A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Composing Linear Layers from Irreducibles by the same authors. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison; v3 also includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM layer-replacement experiments with perplexity and accuracy results, architectural sensitivity experiments, and synthetic convergence experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds end-to-end training results for dense and rotor-based MLPs on Fashion-MNIST.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, bivector-to-rotor construction, generalized two-rotor modules, pooling, and grade-mixing components are retained. The Fashion-MNIST experiment applies the existing rotor machinery in another architecture without documenting a revised method.

E1.justification: v3 adds Fashion-MNIST image classification, substantially extending coverage beyond the language benchmarks and synthetic rotor experiments in v1. Existing Wikitext2, C4, PTB, ARC Challenge, HellaSwag, and appendix evaluations are retained.

E2.justification: The matched LLM comparisons retain the original dense models, LR1, LR4, and BH1. The new Fashion-MNIST comparison reuses the dense-layer alternative in an MLP setting; no new approximation method or comparator change within a retained experiment is reported.

E3.justification: Alongside the unchanged layerwise LLM approximation protocol, v3 introduces joint training from scratch of two-hidden-layer MLPs, replacing every dense layer except the classification head. Evaluation spans ten epochs with validation-selected learning rates. This substantially changes the training regime tested; FLOPs and relative inference runtime are also newly reported.

E4.justification: v3 adds computational-efficiency analysis and compares dense versus rotor learning dynamics across Fashion-MNIST epochs. The existing width/depth sensitivity experiment in Figure 5 and warm-start convergence analysis in Figure 6 are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report Figure 6 averages over 50 runs with one-standard-deviation error bars and the same five random selections for aggregated multilayer results. v3 adds no uncertainty estimates for Fashion-MNIST; its checklist newly explains the existing omission of accuracy error bars.

E6.justification: v3 adds findings about joint training and computational cost: Table 3 reports ten epochs of Fashion-MNIST accuracy, ending at 88.36% for rotors and 89.67% for dense layers. Section 5.2 adds width/depth-dependent FLOP estimates and runtime comparisons. Matched LLM scores and parameter-count tables remain unchanged, so these are new results rather than improved scores under retained settings.

T1.justification: Fact 1 in v3 adds the formal restriction n ≥ 3 to the Spin(n) double-cover statement. The decomposition theorems, parameter-count bounds, and mathematical proofs in Appendix B are substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the algebraic decomposition, parameter-efficiency, and competitive LLM-performance claims. The revised conclusion additionally claims feasibility of joint training from scratch, specifically supported by the new Fashion-MNIST experiment.

C2.justification: Section 3 now explicitly states that the construction does not capture arbitrary linear maps, materially clarifying applicability. v3 also develops the compute-versus-memory-bandwidth argument, gives a concrete statistical-regression application sketch, and interprets slower Fashion-MNIST learning as potentially related to compression. These extend the earlier interpretations and limitations substantially.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-code URL and availability statement, plus Fashion-MNIST architecture and learning-rate details: dense hidden dimension 512, rotor Cl(15), width 3, depth 1, and selected rates 0.002 and 0.005 respectively. Existing LLM hyperparameters and hardware disclosures are retained. External code availability is not independently established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Gallier and Quaintance, Doran and Lasenby, Fashion-MNIST, Tucker tensor regression, and Davies et al. on inference bottlenecks. These support mathematical attribution and limited extensions of application positioning; the existing related-work discussion is largely retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. v3 adds experiment and compute-cost paragraphs, expands and renames the conclusion, inserts acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist, and makes terminology, author-block, and wording corrections.

P2.justification: v3 adds the Fashion-MNIST epoch table and a dashed base-model perplexity reference at 9.845 in Figure 5, with an expanded caption. Existing tables are renumbered or repositioned, and conference formatting changes the front matter and page flow; the other scientific displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the paper through a joint-training test on Fashion-MNIST, an explicit expressivity qualification, clearer compute tradeoffs, and additional reproducibility information. The gain is limited: the core LLM results and proofs remain unchanged, while the new small MLP experiment lacks uncertainty estimates and does not establish full-LLM training or practical speedups.
